note: Irregularities, conflicts between two official sources, and values that could not be confirmed. Each is published on the Flagged for review page with its source links and the manual step that would close it. Flags never block publication; they tell a reader what not to trust yet. Numbering is continuous across sessions, and a resolved flag is kept rather than deleted so the audit trail survives.

flags.title: Submitted tokens are 9 characters, not 10
flags.detail: All five submitted tokens (B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3, B00hJ57DV, B0c8moW59, B0f3GKalj) are 9 characters long. Amazon's own Associates Central help now settles what an ASIN is: 'ASIN is the 10-digit code that Amazon uses to denote specific products' (S18, fetched in full 2026-11-20). None of the five tokens is 10 characters, so none of them is an ASIN, and none can be used in the documented simple-text-link format amazon.com/dp/ASIN/ref=nosim?tag=YOURASSOCIATEID. The five observed product identifiers are all 10 characters, which is consistent with them being ASINs. Because the token is not the identifier, the intended ASIN for each row cannot be derived from the submitted link, so the intended ASIN, official listing URL, confirmation date and confirmation source stay blank on every row.
flags.manual_step: Confirm the intended product for each submitted link in Associates Central (or in the Amazon product page you intended) and supply the full 10-character ASIN or product URL.
flags.resolution_note: Partially settled 2026-11-20: the definition of an ASIN is no longer in question (S18). What remains open is which product the owner meant each token to point at - that needs a signed-in check, tracked as discovery task D-01 and FLG-031.

flags.title: Observed destination ASIN differs from the token in the link
flags.detail: The short links resolved to different 10-character ASINs than the submitted token (for example B04G1MEwY resolved to B0CDY277D3). The observed destinations are recorded in separate fields and are not treated as the intended product. The site links to the observed destination only as a tagged, observed product (see FLG-005).
flags.manual_step: Open each submitted short link in a signed-in browser and confirm the product shown. Confirm whether the intended product is the observed product before it is published as the buy link.

flags.title: Compliance status of the supplied short links is unresolved
flags.detail: The short links are not claimed to be invalid. Associates Program Policies Participation Requirements (w) restrict a link-shortening service in a manner that makes it unclear that the link goes to an Amazon Site (S02). Whether the link.amazon short links fall within that restriction has not been determined. The site does not use the short links for outbound links; they appear only as source evidence. Added 2026-11-20: Amazon's Associates help (S13) states that Amazon full links and Amazon short links are supported in the OneLink setup, and that third-party shortened links are not. Participation Requirements 2(a) requires the Associates tag as a parameter in each Special Link (S02). None of the four observed product redirects contains a tag parameter (see products). Attribution of the link.amazon links to shopnow047c-20 therefore remains unconfirmed, and this flag stays open.
flags.manual_step: Check the supplied short links against Associates Program Policies (w) and the Associates tracking reports. Decide whether to keep them as evidence only or to replace them completely.

flags.title: One submitted link (B00hJ57DV) initially appeared not to resolve to a product
flags.detail: The link landed on an Amazon 'Continue shopping' checkpoint page with no product title, price or ASIN. The fetch was not a signed-in browser session, so the result may depend on session, region or timing. No product is shown for this row and no buy link is published. — RESOLVED 2026-11-20: this link does resolve; see resolution field.
flags.manual_step: Open the link in a signed-in browser. Supply the intended product URL if it can be identified.
flags.resolution: Superseded 2026-11-20: B00hJ57DV was re-fetched and resolved to B08DKYBTPH (Chefman 8 Qt TurboFry). The earlier "Continue shopping" checkpoint was an intermittent bot-check, not a dead link. Kept for the audit trail rather than deleted. Check it by hand: https://link.amazon/B00hJ57DV should land on https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08DKYBTPH

flags.title: Tagged Special Links are not yet validated in Associates Central
flags.detail: The outbound links use the Associates tracking ID shopnow047c-20 in the /dp/ format (?tag=). Operating Agreement §1 defines Special Links as links in the tagged formats Amazon provides, and Participation Requirements §2 requires the tag as a URL parameter (S01, S02). The links have not been generated or tested in Associates Central, and no tracking report has been reviewed, because the sandbox has no Associates login. Gate G-02 requires one link per product to be validated before any scaling.
flags.manual_step: Sign in to Associates Central, generate one Special Link per observed product with the enrolled tracking ID, click it, confirm the destination and the tracking report, then mark G-02 done.

flags.title: Associates account status and declared site are unknown
flags.detail: Associates help states that tags must be embedded in links on the sites declared in the application (S11). The declared site URL and account approval status are unknown to this build. The qualifying-sales requirement (three within 180 days) is also stated (S11).
flags.manual_step: Confirm that the Associates account declares the GitHub Pages URL (https://karagemop466-tech.github.io/Affil3/) or a custom domain for it, and that the account is active.

flags.title: Content depth is below the official 'robust content' rule of thumb
flags.detail: The Associates help text says a rule of thumb is at least 10 posts (S11). The site has 5 guides and 5 product rows. Adding content is a decision for the user (see suggestion S-07).
flags.manual_step: Decide the content plan (suggestion S-07) before submitting the site for Associates review.

flags.title: Measurement events were not defined in the brief
flags.detail: The brief asks to 'record the five defined events' but does not list them. This build proposes five events: page_view, category_view, product_view, outbound_click, guide_read_75. They are not confirmed.
flags.manual_step: Confirm or replace the five events (question Q-05).

flags.title: Analytics endpoint is not deployed; analytics is inactive on the live site
flags.detail: GitHub Pages serves static files and cannot run the collector. The client code is present but sends nothing until an endpoint is configured in data/config.json. The collector (tools/collector.mjs) is self-hostable. No clicks or conversions are being recorded on the live site yet.
flags.manual_step: Choose a hosting option for the collector (suggestion S-03). Then set analyticsEndpoint in data/config.json and rebuild.

flags.title: Disclosure placement needs manual review on real devices
flags.detail: The disclosure strip is placed under the masthead on every page and repeated in the footer, using the statement required by Operating Agreement §5 (S01). FTC guidance asks that disclosures be placed where they are hard to miss and near the link (S07, S08). Automated checks confirm presence, not visibility on a phone.
flags.manual_step: Open the live site on a phone-sized screen and confirm the strip is visible without scrolling on the home page and on a guide page.

flags.title: Tracking ID format matches Associates convention; ownership not confirmed
flags.detail: shopnow047c-20 ends in -20, the form Associates help describes for the US program (S03). The sandbox cannot confirm that the ID belongs to the signed-in account.
flags.manual_step: In Associates Central, confirm that shopnow047c-20 is listed as a tracking ID on the account.

flags.title: No Amazon-owned ASIN definition was retrieved (resolved)
flags.detail: Searches returned third-party explanations of ASINs. No Amazon-owned definitional page was located, so the 10-character rule is supported only by the observed amazon.com identifiers (S04) and secondary sources.
flags.resolution: Resolved 2026-11-20. The manual step was met: Associates Central's own help page 'How do I build a simple text link to a specific item on Amazon?' states 'ASIN is the 10-digit code that Amazon uses to denote specific products' and gives the /dp/ASIN/ref=nosim?tag= link format. Added to the source register as S18 and quoted there. The 10-character rule no longer depends on secondary sources or on the observed identifiers.

flags.title: Google Search Console is not connected
flags.detail: The sitemap and feed are generated, and robots.txt references the sitemap. Search Console ownership verification needs a signed-in Google account, which the sandbox does not have. No verification token has been created or added.
flags.manual_step: Add the site as a URL-prefix property in Search Console, verify it, and submit sitemap.xml.

flags.title: Author is a team byline, not a named person
flags.detail: No named author, credential or biography is supplied, so the site uses 'Affil3 editorial team'. Inventing a person would be a fabrication.
flags.manual_step: Decide on a named author and bio (suggestion S-06).

flags.title: No product imagery is used
flags.detail: Amazon product images are Program Content. The IP License limits use of Program Content to the Associates purposes (S02), so the site uses typography and no product photography. Imagery is a decision (suggestion S-05).
flags.manual_step: Decide the imagery approach (suggestion S-05).

flags.title: Prices, ratings and availability are not recorded
flags.detail: Prices and ratings were visible only in carousel items on the fetched pages, not as confirmed values for the observed product. They change over time. Nothing is recorded or displayed, so no unverified number appears on the site.
flags.manual_step: If prices are wanted, decide the approach (suggestion S-10) and capture them only with a dated observation from an authorized source.

flags.title: Parallel sessions claim the same task on separate branches
flags.detail: Five other arena/*-affil3 branches on origin each claim the same overall task and each has its own COORDINATION.md. They were read (not modified) to check for overlap. Merging them to main will conflict. This branch builds at the repository root and uses its own file names to limit collisions, but a single integration branch should be chosen by the user. The other session's site (PR #1) is preserved unchanged at legacy/arena-83a43a96/ and is not linked from this site.
flags.manual_step: Choose which branch becomes the integration branch, or close the others.

flags.title: Repository review: the starting repo had only a one-line README
flags.detail: The repository had one commit with a README.md containing '# Affil3'. No code, data, configuration or history beyond that was present, so there were no existing irregularities to review.
flags.manual_step: None.

flags.title: Branch naming request differs from the session rule
flags.detail: The brief asks for session-<id>/<task> branches. This session may only work on its assigned branch, arena/6249757a-affil3, so all work is committed there and the PR is opened from it.
flags.manual_step: None unless you want a different naming policy.

flags.title: GitHub Pages source could not be changed from this session
flags.detail: The sandbox token returned HTTP 403 ('Resource not accessible by integration') when switching Pages to main /docs. Pages therefore serves main at the repository root. To publish one site without changing settings, this site is generated at the repository root and the earlier root-level site (PR #1) was moved, unchanged, to legacy/arena-83a43a96/. Nothing was deleted. To serve a different folder, change Settings > Pages.
flags.manual_step: Optional: if you prefer the site under /docs, change Settings > Pages > Source to main /docs, then remove the root copies.

flags.title: Thermometer guide omitted the FSIS ground-meat row; corrected
flags.detail: The guide 'Is your meat thermometer telling you the right number?' listed beef, poultry and ham minimums but omitted the FSIS row 'Ground Meats: 160 degrees F'. Corrected on 2026-11-20 by adding 'Ground meats: 160 °F.' to the list, matching the FSIS chart. The other listed values (beef/pork/veal/lamb 145 °F with a 3-minute rest; ground poultry 165 °F; all poultry 165 °F; uncooked ham 145 °F with a 3-minute rest) were checked against the same chart and match. Probe-placement statements for whole poultry were checked against the FSIS Food Thermometers factsheet and match.

flags.title: Two product destinations were transposed in the root-site register (corrected)
flags.detail: data/products.json recorded B08DKYBTPH (Chefman 8 Qt air fryer) as the destination of B0c8moW59, and recorded B00hJ57DV as unresolved. Both were wrong. Re-fetched twice on 2026-11-20: B00hJ57DV resolves to B08DKYBTPH and B0c8moW59 resolves to B0DHZTCNR5 (ThermoMaven 1 Sec meat thermometer). The two destinations had been swapped between the two rows. The editorial register at data/register/products.json reached the same destinations by a separate session, which corroborates the correction. Both records now carry a "reverification" block preserving the earlier value, so the fix is auditable rather than silent.
flags.impact: Before the fix the root site attributed a meat thermometer to the wrong submitted link, listed an air fryer as unresolved, and had two category assignments wrong.
flags.resolution: P03 and P04 corrected in data/products.json; previous values retained in each record's reverification block. FLG-004 marked resolved. Category pages, shop table and guide cross-links regenerated. Check both by hand: https://link.amazon/B00hJ57DV should land on https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08DKYBTPH, and https://link.amazon/B0c8moW59 should land on https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DHZTCNR5
flags.detected_by: session arena/166bf329-affil3, cross-checking independently resolved short links against the stored register

flags.title: CHEF iQ battery life: the manufacturer's own pages disagree
flags.detail: The CHEF iQ Sense product page states '70+ Hours of Battery'. The CHEF iQ Sense FAQ on the same domain states that Gen 3 probes hold a charge for 'up to 60 hours'. Both are official CHEF iQ pages, so this site publishes no battery figure at all rather than choosing the friendlier one. The ambient temperature range, sensor count and probe dimensions on the product page are not in dispute and are published.
flags.impact: One marketing figure is unusable. No other specification is affected.
flags.manual_step: Ask CHEF iQ support which figure applies to the Gen 3 unit sold under B0DZFD6R9Z, or leave the battery field blank.

flags.title: Emeril Lagasse 26 QT: preset and accessory counts differ across official pages
flags.detail: The Emeril Everyday product page shows '25 Cooking Pre-sets' in its specification strip and '24 one-touch cooking presets' in its own description, and an image on the same page reads '11-in-1'. The Amazon listing title says '24 One-Touch Preset Options' and 'Six Cooking Accessories Included', while the manufacturer description mentions seven. Because the official sources conflict, this site publishes no preset count and no accessory count.
flags.impact: Two secondary specifications are withheld. Capacity, dimensions and form factor are unaffected.
flags.manual_step: Check the printed quick-start guide in the box, which is the only source that decides it for a shipped unit.

flags.title: ThermoMaven: no manufacturer page, so every specification is withheld
flags.detail: No manufacturer product page for the ThermoMaven thermometer could be located. Its accuracy, certification and waterproofing claims exist only on the marketplace listing. The site therefore shows the product as context, with no buy button and no specifications at all, rather than promoting listing copy to a verified fact.
flags.impact: One of five products is present but not recommended, and carries no outbound link.
flags.manual_step: If ThermoMaven publishes a product page for this model, supply the URL and the specification table can be filled and re-verified.

flags.title: The 8 Qt air fryer listing and the manufacturer page describe two different machines
flags.detail: The Amazon listing for B08DKYBTPH states, in its own 'About this item' copy, that the unit is 1000 W/120 V, model RJ38-SQSS-8T, with a 200-400 °F range, a 12.75 x 13.5 x 10 in body and a stainless-steel finish. Chefman's own product page for the 8 Qt model with Hi-Fry describes RJ38-8T-BLACK, 1700 W/120 V, up to 450 °F, and a matte-black finish. Both cannot describe the same appliance. This site therefore publishes capacity (8 qt, which both agree on) and withholds wattage, temperature range, dimensions and finish. The listing's figures are shown in a separate column so a reader can see both without either being presented as verified.
flags.impact: Four specifications are withheld on the 8 Qt product page. Readers are told why. This is the single most consequential data conflict found on the site.
flags.manual_step: Confirm which model ships from the listing, by checking the model number printed on the unit or the box, or by asking Chefman support whether RJ38-SQSS-8T and RJ38-8T-BLACK share a listing.

flags.title: The same listing carries two different temperature ranges in two places
flags.detail: In the 'About this item' bullets the Amazon listing for B08DKYBTPH describes a 200-400 °F range and a 1000 W element, while the listing title advertises a '450°F Hi-Fry option'. A Hi-Fry burst and a 400 °F ceiling can coexist if Hi-Fry is a separate short-lived mode, but the listing never explains it. Because the two statements are not reconcilable from the page alone, no temperature figure is published for this product.
flags.impact: Temperature is withheld on one product.
flags.manual_step: The user guide linked from the listing should settle it. Read it and supply the page reference.

flags.title: Amazon links were published without the tracking tag, including the citations
flags.detail: Program Policies 2(b) requires the Associates ID as a URL parameter on every link placed on the site, not only on buy buttons. The site linked the observed Amazon page in the source column of the shop table and on product pages, and published the supplied link.amazon short links as clickable links, none of which carried tag=shopnow047c-20.
flags.manual_step: None. The build now enforces the rule on every page: any link to an Amazon retail host gets the tag and rel=sponsored, and a link.amazon short link is rendered as text because it cannot carry the tag.
flags.resolution: Build-level link policy added and asserted by the gate on every page (retail Amazon link must carry the tag; no short link may be published as a link). Check count rose from 1,610 to 2,805.

flags.title: Every thermometer page referenced an image that was never committed
flags.detail: Fourteen references pointed at /assets/img/hero-thermometer.jpg, which did not exist in the repository. The category page, both thermometer product pages, the guides index and the thermometer guide would have shown a broken image on the live site.
flags.manual_step: None. The image was created in the same photographic style as the other hero images and committed; the gate now checks that every referenced image exists, is served locally, and has alt text.
flags.resolution: Image added on 2026-11-20. The image check was added to the gate, so a missing image fails the build from now on.

flags.title: Independent fetch by session arena63534e5d corroborated the corrected P03/P04 mapping
flags.detail: During the publication polish pass, an unauthenticated fetch observed B00hJ57DV resolving to B08DKYBTPH (Chefman 8 Qt) and B0c8moW59 landing on an intermittent checkpoint. Both observations agree with the corrected register: P03's mapping to B08DKYBTPH was confirmed independently, and P04's checkpoint matches the intermittent behavior recorded in FLG-004/FLG-022 rather than a dead link. Draft numbers this flag previously held on the session branch (FLG-021, FLG-023, FLG-028) all belong to other sessions' published findings, so it is recorded here as FLG-028's successor number FLG-030.

flags.title: Five short links did not resolve to product pages on re-check; the token-to-ASIN mapping is not reproducible unauthenticated
flags.detail: On 2026-11-20 the final integration session fetched each submitted short link again, without a signed-in browser and without an Associates session. Both link.amazon links that were reachable landed on the Amazon home page (https://www.amazon.com/, title 'Amazon.com. Spend less. Smile more.') with no product title, no ASIN and no breadcrumb. The other three short links could not be reached from the sandbox at all, because the TLS handshake to link.amazon was refused; those three are untested, not failed. This does not reproduce the token-to-ASIN mapping recorded by earlier sessions, and it does not disprove it either. Three different results have now been recorded for the same links: product pages, an intermittent 'Continue shopping' checkpoint, and the Amazon home page. The mapping therefore depends on session, region or bot-check state and cannot be certified from an unauthenticated fetch. No published field changed: every intended ASIN stays blank, and every buy link points at an observed ASIN that was verified directly rather than through the short link (see the same-day observation record).
flags.manual_step: Open each short link once in a browser signed in to the Associates account with cookies accepted, and record the ASIN that appears in the URL. If it lands on the home page again, use Associates Central's link report instead, which shows the destination for a tracked link.

flags.title: The site publishes 5 guides; Amazon describes a rule of thumb of at least 10 posts
flags.detail: Associates Central's application review help page states: 'All Sites must have robust original content (even when advertising is removed) - a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts.' This site publishes five guides plus five product pages, a shop table, a categories index and the governance pages. On a strict guide count that is five against a stated rule of thumb of ten. The rule of thumb is not a hard threshold and Amazon reviews the site as a whole, so this is recorded as a gap rather than a failure. The related requirement that site content be recent within roughly 60 days is tracked by publishing cadence (suggestion S-05).
flags.impact: None on what is published today. It bounds how the site should be described: the compliance page states the count plainly instead of implying the site already meets the bar.
flags.manual_step: Publish the next five guides on the cadence chosen in S-05, then re-read this flag. Choosing topics from Search Console queries (discovery task D-09) is the intended source rather than instinct.
